INDIVIDUAL SPECIES GUIDE · NOT A STOCK LISTING

Black-headed Caique

The Black-headed Caique is a compact, boldly marked South American parrot with a black crown, orange-yellow collar and green wings. Its energetic curiosity brings plenty of activity, and demands safe play, supervision and patient training.

Scientific namePionites melanocephalus
Typical adult sizeAbout 23 cm long; around 130–170 g, with individual variation.
Lifetime planningOften several decades; estimates differ, so plan for a long-term companion.

Overview and appearance

Black-headed Caiques have a dark cap, orange-yellow cheeks and throat, green wings and a white belly. Their short, stocky shape and lively movement distinguish them from longer-tailed parrots. They occur in northern South America and are adapted to active foraging and movement through forest environments.

A caique’s compact frame does not mean its energy can be contained in a small cage. It benefits from safe climbing, foot play, food searching and interaction. Their agility makes supervision important wherever they explore beyond an enclosure.

Personality and social needs

Caiques are often described as exuberant, curious and physically playful. Individual energy and handling preferences still vary. A bird may wrestle with safe toys or investigate objects, but play should be structured so that it does not include rough contact with people or unsafe household items.

Regular social contact matters, alongside practice settling and playing independently. Introductions to other birds should be gradual, with separate secure spaces and close management. Do not assume a confident caique will automatically be compatible with another pet.

Typical adult size

Black-headed Caiques are around 23 cm long and often weigh roughly 130–170 g. As with all ranges, individual build differs. Enclosure bar spacing must be appropriate for a small parrot, while the interior should still allow climbing, hopping and movement among varied perches.

Expected lifespan and long-term care

Caiques are long-lived companions, potentially requiring care for several decades. Exact expectations vary between references and individuals. Plan for long-term housing, routine care and a future caregiver if your circumstances change.

Talking and vocalisation

Caiques can be busy and vocal, with calls, whistles and contact sounds. Their volume and frequency depend on the individual and situation. Do not choose one based on a promise that small parrots are quiet or that a particular bird will talk.

Intelligence and reward-based training

Their curiosity can make reward-based learning fun and useful. Practise target training, calm stationing and voluntary carrier entry in short sessions. Puzzle feeders, supervised foot toys and safe foraging turn energy into problem-solving. Teach clear routines and avoid encouraging nipping or rough play for amusement.

Diet and nutrition

Offer appropriate formulated food with a variety of fresh vegetables and other produce; use rich treats and seeds thoughtfully. A seed-only diet is not a balanced default. Consult an avian veterinarian about the individual’s current food, body condition and any transition rather than applying a fixed diet prescription.

Housing, exercise and enrichment

Give the bird a secure enclosure with climbing opportunities, varied perches and safe materials to chew. Provide supervised exercise and rotate enrichment frequently to maintain interest. Caiques explore with their beaks and feet, so check toys, flooring and play areas for small hazards.

Suitability and ownership questions

A Black-headed Caique may suit an active, attentive home that can channel its physical play and curious nature into safe routines. It needs more than occasional cuddles and may not suit a household looking for a calm, hands-off bird. Families need adults to supervise activity and teach children gentle boundaries.

Before enquiring, ask about age, current diet, daily routine, play style and handling preferences. Discuss safe exercise and interaction with other pets, plus current individual availability. This profile is species education, not confirmation that a Black-headed Caique is in stock.
